messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@ausoft.com>

Cc: procurement@ausoft.com, Ausoft Legal <legal@ausoft.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Ausoft - SLA redlines for MSA + Order Form

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our procurement team's working SLA redlines for the MSA and Order Form (See: Ausoft_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf). High level asks:

- Uptime: 99.95% across production endpoints (we've proposed measurement windows and aggregation rules in the attachment).
- Service credits: linear step-down with a 3x monthly spend cap (we included examples).
- Response times: P1 30 minutes, P2 4 hours, P3 24 hours — measured business hours.
- Maintenance: a request to limit rolling maintenance to a single 4-hour weekly blackout per region and require 72-hour notice for any planned upgrades that may impact availability.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these changes, or propose a counter with the areas you cannot meet? Legal is looped in on the attachment. We are hoping to finalize language and route to DocuSign by EOD Thursday (AUS time).

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Procurement, Ausoft

Date: 2026-08-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ausoft - SLA redlines for MSA + Order Form

Sarah — thanks for the detailed redlines and examples. We reviewed the attachment and can move quickly on this. A few immediate notes:

- Uptime: 99.95% is aggressive for our multi-region HA pattern on some of the larger embeddings workloads; we can propose a tiered approach (99.95 for core API endpoints, 99.90 for batch/embeddings endpoints) with documented measurement methods.
- Service credits: we typically cap at 1x monthly spend (we can explain the rationale), but are open to a compromise using a stepped multiplier tied to outage severity.
- Response times: P1 60 minutes (on-call rotation), P2 4 hours, P3 24 hours — we can accept the P2/P3 as-is if P1 is 60 minutes.
- Maintenance: 72-hour notice is fine; limiting to one 4-hour weekly blackout per region is doable but we need flexibility for emergency security patches with shorter notice and a defined backstop.

I'll pull the proposed language together and loop Legal (Marissa + Laura) to prepare a counter. If Ausoft can sign off on the tiered uptime approach and a 1.5x service-credit compromise, we can prepare a DocuSign packet by tomorrow morning.

I'll follow up internally now with proposed wording.

Best,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: chloe.martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Ausoft - SLA redlines for MSA + Order Form

Folks — forwarding Sarah's attachment + asks. Quick internal alignment request before I send a counter:

1) Uptime tiers: propose the following language for Order Form/SLA:
   - "Core API endpoints" (model inference, REST chat/generate) measured per region: 99.95% monthly uptime.
   - "Auxiliary services" (async batch embeddings, bulk ingestion) measured per region: 99.90% monthly uptime.

2) Credits cap: recommend we offer step-down credits with a monthly cap at 1.5x monthly service fees and an aggregate annual cap equal to 3x monthly fees. This is a middle ground vs their 3x request.

3) Response Tiers: accept P2/P3 as requested; P1 to remain 60 minutes with guaranteed on-call rotation and target response SLAs documented in the runbook.

4) Maintenance: accept 72-hour notice for planned work; limit routine maintenance to 1x 4-hour weekly blackout per region. For emergency security patches we will provide as much notice as possible and will offer a post-event RCA. Recommend we add a carveout clause that emergency patches (CVSS >= 8.0) may proceed with 6-hour notice if safety is at risk.

Any objections? Marissa/Laura, can you draft the redline into a doc I can send to Sarah? Aditya, flag anything infra-side we can't commit to.

—Chloe

Chloe — thanks. Drafted counter language and put it into RI_SLA_Counter_v1.docx (see attached). High-level changes in the doc:

- Concrete uptime measurement paragraph with aggregation windows and excluded maintenance periods.
- Step-down credit table that peaks at 1.5x monthly spend and a 3x annual backstop; examples in the table illustrate partial-credit calculations.
- Response definitions that keep P1 at 60 minutes but define "severity" criteria more narrowly so we don't over-classify incidents as P1.
- Emergency maintenance carveout for critical security fixes (CVSS >=8) that allows 6-hour notice and requires an RCA within 72 hours.

Laura: legal clean-up on indemnities and wording for "excluded causes" would be appreciated. Aditya: confirm that the maintenance carveout is operationally feasible — particularly the 6-hour emergency pathway.

Attaching RI_SLA_Counter_v1.docx for review.

—Marissa

Subject: Proposed counter: SLA and maintenance carveouts (Ausoft) — next steps

Sarah — attaching our proposed counter (RI_SLA_Counter_v1.docx). Summary of the final positions in the doc:

- Uptime: tiered measurement — Core API 99.95% / Auxiliary 99.90% (monthly measurement per region).
- Credits: step-down model with examples; monthly cap at 1.5x monthly fees and an annual aggregate cap at 3x monthly fees.
- P1 Response: 60 minute on-call target (we've tightened severity criteria).
- Maintenance: 72-hour notice for planned work, routine weekly 4-hour blackout per region, emergency carveout (CVSS >=8) with 6-hour notice + RCA within 72 hours.

If that language looks acceptable, we will prepare an Order Form and route the MSA/Order Form package through DocuSign. To speed things up we've pre-populated the DocuSign packet; if Ausoft is good with the counter I can send the packet to your procurement and legal contacts by EOD.

DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.com/embedded/XYZ-abc-987
Working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bSLA-Working-Docs

As a reminder, the only non-negotiable for us is the emergency security carveout; it's critical for timely patches. Otherwise the rest is a compromise on both sides.

Next steps (requested):
- Sarah: confirm acceptance of the tiered uptime approach and the 1.5x monthly credit cap by EOD tomorrow.
- Ausoft Legal: if you prefer redline edits, we can ingest them and route back within 24 hours.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-minute call if that helps finalize language.

Best,
Chloe

2) The 1.5x monthly credit cap is acceptable to procurement; legal will send a couple of tiny redline edits to the maintenance carveout language (phrasing and RCA timing).
